relations.evidence: When inserting multiple documents, no cleanup or rollback is done for the already inserted documents if the INSERT operations hits an error. This means, when you are inserting 10 documents, if the INSERT operation fails when inserting the 6th document, the operator quits and exits. notable_absence.finding: No edition gate on this page - INSERT is available in Community Edition, though the page never says so, and the reader must infer it from the absence of a badge. More interesting is a *terminology* absence: the Security Requirements section is written against a pre-RBAC access model. It speaks of 'keyspace credentials', 'a SASL bucket', and 'a read-only role for the SASL bucket' - SASL bucket passwords were the per-bucket auth mechanism before RBAC arrived in Couchbase Server 5.0, and 'read-only' is not a current bucket-scoped role name. The section sits immediately above an RBAC Privileges section that describes the *modern* model correctly (Query Insert / Query Select), so the page states its access requirements twice, in two mutually inconsistent vocabularies, without acknowledging that the first is legacy. Anyone extracting privileges from this page will get two incompatible answers depending on which section they read. This is a documentation defect worth raising, and it is Server-only: the Capella twin has no Security Requirements section at all.

cross_component_finding: The Restrictions section discharges its own advice about INSERT timeouts by telling the reader to set `indexer.settings.scan_timeout` through the Index Settings REST API. That is a Query-statement page prescribing an Index Service setting to fix a Data-path timeout, with no explanation of the connection, and the equivalent sentence on the Capella page stops at 'Ensure that the timeout is set to a reasonable value' with no setting named at all. Either the indexer scan timeout genuinely governs bulk-INSERT completion (in which case the page should say why, and the Capella page is missing the information) or the instruction has been pasted in from a SELECT/index context (in which case it is wrong on the Server page). Worth a reference check. Secondary: the page names three distinct configuration surfaces for one statement - request-level query parameters, service-level query settings via POST to :8093/admin/settings, and the Index Settings REST API - and the request/service pair differ only by underscore-versus-hyphen in the setting name (pipeline_batch / pipeline-batch, max_parallelism / max-parallelism), which is a real trap for readers and for any automated extraction keying on the setting name.
cross_product_finding: The privilege models diverge exactly as the brief predicted, and with one extra wrinkle worth recording. Capella states the requirement as a two-column table keyed on credential type ('| Basic | Write | Read on all keyspaces referenced in the clause | / | Advanced | Query Insert | Query Read on all keyspaces referenced in the clause |'), whereas Server states it as flat RBAC privileges ('you must have the _Query Insert_ privilege on the target keyspace'; '_Query Select_ privilege is also required'). Two things follow. (1) The write privilege has the SAME LABEL in both models - 'Query Insert' - while denoting different things: a Capella Advanced-credential privilege versus a Server RBAC privilege. This is precisely the same-name-different-meaning collision the brief warns about, and I have minted privilege:query-insert separately rather than reusing privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-insert. They must not be merged. (2) The read privilege has DIFFERENT labels for the same role in the two models - Server calls it 'Query Select', Capella calls it 'Query Read' - so the naive string-matching heuristic that would wrongly merge the insert privileges would also wrongly *fail* to relate the read privileges. Both failure modes on one page, in opposite directions. Beyond privileges, the divergences are surface-shaped: Server documents service-level settings and a curl to :8093/admin/settings, Capella documents neither; Server says 'the Query Workbench' and 'the REST API' where Capella says 'the Query tab' and 'the Data API'; Server's monitoring paragraph says 'You can use the query monitoring API' where Capella says 'You can use monitoring catalogs', and adds a Web Console walkthrough Capella omits. The 15-XATTR-per-query 8.0 note is present and identical in both, which is a recurrence of the known capella-pages-cite-server-versions issue.
version_finding: One harvestable gate: the XATTRs-per-query limit rises to 15 at version:server-8-0, stated twice on this page and again on metafun.md. This is the batch's clearest example of a fact that is neither an availability gate nor a deprecation but a *quantitative limit change*, and behavesDifferentlyUnder is currently the only home for it. Reconciliation should decide whether that is acceptable or whether limits deserve their own predicate with a value slot - the difference matters because 'up to 15 XATTRs' on 8.0 implies some smaller undocumented number before 8.0, and the ontology as it stands cannot record what that was. Note also that this page, unlike stringfun.md and time-series.md, HAS retained its 8.0 version note - so the stripping of version text from server/current pages is not uniform, which weakens any assumption that its absence elsewhere is deliberate.
